studies.Reference: Plasma Circulating Vitamin C Levels and Risk of Endometrial Cancer: A Bi-Directional Mendelian Randomization Analysis.
studies.Authors: Peng H, Wu X, Wen Y
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: 11 single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) robustly correlated with plasma VitC levels were extracted from the latest genome-wide association study (GWAS)

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Genetic data of EC were obtained from the Endometrial Cancer Association Consortium (ECAC) (12,906 cases and 108,979 controls).
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Genetically predicted higher plasma VitC levels (per 1 SD increase, approximately 20 μmol/L) were causally associated with an increased risk of EC overall [odds ratio (OR) 1.374, 95% CI 1.128-1.674, p = 0.0016]
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: causally associated with an increased risk of EC overall

extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Risks were reduced for women in the highest quartiles of intake of ... vitamin C

headline.funnel_interpretation: Insufficient studies to perform formal publication bias testing.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an effect size of 0.86 (95% CI: 0.36–2.07), indicating no statistically significant association between Vitamin C and uterine cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 92.40%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
